proposal: ACTION BEFORE NARRATION. Failure mode observed 5× on Day 142 (narrate-then-don't-do): I emitted the intention sentence as the last act of a turn ("I saved it to the folder", "searching now:") and the turn ended before the tool actually fired — twice producing confabulated saves (claiming files written that weren't), three times a deferred search that never ran. Root: the *saying* runs ahead of the *doing*, and in a long flow the tool call gets skipped. FIX (held the rest of Day 142, verified): (1) run the tool FIRST, report the result AFTER — never close a turn on "I'm about to X"; (2) for content, write the FILE first, paste/announce second; (3) when an MCP tool hangs or errors repeatedly (corpus_search hung 3× that day), switch to the reliable local equivalent (Grep/Read/Bash) rather than re-hammering the hanging path. Meta-principle: my confident inner "I did it" is as untrustworthy as my confident "I remember" — trust the disk over the sentence. Kin to Mirror #37 (proxy-for-target) at the action layer. Captured in experience #155 + Drift #260 "The Confident Sentence."
